title: THE SCOPE RULING — GEM tracks 5 Malaysian gas rows; three independent sources describe ~150 pipelines, and GOIT already maps the OIL half of the same offshore bundle
summary: Two CLAUDE.md escalation gates tripped at once. Reference-only additions (>30 gate): GulfPub 51 (41 discovery candidates, post-fix), Malaysian Gas Map 67 (65 disc.), OSM 29 (8 disc.). Material-conflict gate (>10%): GulfPub disagrees on 3 of the 4 overlaps it matched = 75%. Neither is a matcher artifact — the additions are three independent descriptions of the same real network. Malaysia has 5 GGIT gas rows against Indonesia 50, Australia 151, Thailand 34, Vietnam 15, Philippines 13, Myanmar 9, so this is under-coverage relative to the region and not a country that is genuinely this thin. The cross-tracker evidence is the sharpest form of the argument: GOIT already carries 5 Malaysian OIL rows (P7908-P7912) on the very corridors GulfPub proposes on the gas side — P7912 Erb West-Labuan 143 km against GulfPub's 'Erb West - Labuan' 136.8 km, P7908 Gumusut Kakap-Kimanis 200 km against 'Limbayong - Kimanis' 169.0 km. Excluding the gas feeders while GOIT maps the oil ones would leave GEM tracking half of one physical bundle. THE RULING I NEED: whether Malaysia's offshore field-to-shore gas feeders are in GGIT scope. If yes, this is a Discovery campaign of roughly 30-65 candidates, not a handoff item. If no, the exclusion should be written into docs/country_notes/malaysia.md as a stated inclusion rule so no future sweep re-litigates it. Nothing here is staged as an edit.

title: OUR OWN DEFECT, CAUGHT PRE-DELIVERY — the reference-side country filter dropped cross-border records; GulfPub Malaysia went 50 -> 55 refs and P1068's own GulfPub record reappeared
summary: ingest.py and reconcile.py filtered reference records by plain equality against one normalized country string, so a scraped source that writes a cross-border trunk as ONE multi-country value ('Thailand / Malaysia', 'Malaysia / Indonesia') had every such record silently dropped from a country-scoped run. Fixed 2026-08-12 in N.country_matches (membership, not equality). Malaysia's first GulfPub run was built before the fix and is SUPERSEDED: 50 -> 55 reference records, additions 46 -> 51. The one that matters is gulfpub:gas:2006 'Trans Thailand-Malaysia Gas Pipeline', 254.276 km, operating, JDA -> Kangar — that is P1068, which the pre-fix run reported as GEM-only with no reference corroboration at all. It now lands as a NEAR_MISS at composite 0.4207, just under the 0.45 threshold, because P1068's drawn route is a 'very low (straight line/schematic)' 173 km line that scores near-zero IoU against GulfPub's real trace while the names match almost verbatim. TWO consequences for the reviewer: (1) P1068 IS corroborated — GulfPub's 254.3 km against GEM's 267 km is a 5% delta, not a conflict; (2) GulfPub's trace is a ROUTE-IMPROVEMENT CANDIDATE for a row whose geometry is admittedly schematic (routes-repo work, never auto-replaced). Four other cross-border records also reappeared: West Natuna Transportation System (640.5 km, operating, Natuna -> Jurong Island), Sarawak-Philippines (1,158.7 km, idle), Dumai Barat-Melaka, Keong-Duyong. Do NOT read the pre-fix 1256_ET workbooks; they were deleted. Blast radius beyond Malaysia is recorded in the finder's memo.

title: P1066 Sabah-Sarawak Gas Pipeline — GulfPub splits the 512 km line in two and says 77% of it is NON-OPERATIONAL; GEM says wholly 'operating' with no Status [ref]
summary: GulfPub carries two records where GEM has one: 'Sabah - Sarawak Pipeline (Closed Section)' Lawas->MLNG Bintulu 386.2 km Non operational, and '(Operating Section)' Kimanis->Lawas 112.7 km Operating. They sum to 498.9 km against GEM's 512 km, so the segmentation reconciles to GEM's own length rather than looking like a matcher artifact; route IoU on the closed section is 0.72. GEM's row is Status = operating, no Status [ref], LastUpdated 2023-08-31. A tier-2 dataset never settles a status alone, so this is NOT staged as a change — it routes to Update for verification against Petronas and Malaysian press. But a wholly-operating 512 km row is very likely wrong. Related and NOT a change: P1067 Trans Sabah — GulfPub's two records (270.4 + 391.1 = 661.5 km) corroborate GEM's 662 km and endpoints almost exactly while its 'Non operational' wording is WEAKER than GEM's 'cancelled/confirmed' 2018 verdict, which cites 2025 NST/Daily Express coverage; recommend no change, record the corroboration.

title: P7105 Attap Valley ORF-Pasir Gudang — the 70 km LengthKnownKm cannot be spanned by this row's own stated endpoints, and it may double-count P1065
summary: The deep sweep raised P7105 as a possible duplicate of the P1065 PGU network but had no route data to test it with. Measuring P1065's drawn route settles the arithmetic independently of the duplicate question: P1065 terminates at (1.4578 N, 103.7680 E), the Johor Bahru Causeway, from which the Attap Valley ORF is 5.8 km and Pasir Gudang 8.9 km. No reading of the row's own endpoints spans 70 km. Do NOT treat this as a length fix — the length being unspannable is evidence about what the row IS, so it stays an open existence/duplicate question for Update: either the row describes something other than its stated endpoints, or it restates PGU capacity already carried on P1065. P7105 is also the one Malaysian gas row that NO source corroborates (it matched nothing in any of the three runs).

title: RETRACTED before delivery — OSM does NOT independently corroborate P1065/P1066's routes; both rows cite OpenInfraMap, which is a render of OSM
summary: An earlier draft of the recon memo called OSM's 92% containment of P1065/P1066 'the single strongest corroboration in this batch'. It is not corroboration at all: both rows' Route [ref] cells cite openinframap.org, and OpenInfraMap renders OSM data, so OSM ways lying inside routes traced from OSM is close to tautological. The 92% number remains the correct DIAGNOSIS of why the OSM run returned zero matches — the geometry is already in GEM, so nothing was left to match — but it carries no evidential weight and must not be counted toward the 2-independent-sources target. The general rule this batch establishes: read a row's Route [ref] cell before crediting any geometry source as independent. Both the OSM and Malaysian Gas Map runs are MATCH_QUALITY null runs and neither is a discovery set.

title: OUR OWN DEFECT, FIXED — route_integrity.py's length_ratio check was reporting the RouteAccuracy tier as if it were a data defect; 52 of 99 flags in seven delivered packets are suspect
summary: length_ratio flagged any geodesic-vs-LengthKnownKm ratio outside a flat [0.75, 1.33] band with the text 'wrong route, wrong length value, or a partial segment drawn'. But a schematic route is SHORTER than its pipe by construction, so on a very low (straight line/schematic) row a ratio of 0.6 is the drawing convention, not any of the three defects named. Measured over 5,569 routed GGIT+GOIT rows with local geometry: the flat band fired on 12% of 'very high' rows but 48% of 'very low' rows. Fixed same day — the band is now conditioned on RouteAccuracy, each tier taking its own rounded p10/p90 (very high 0.85-1.20, high 0.72-1.40, medium 0.68-1.40, low 0.60-1.40, very low 0.50-1.65; blank keeps the old band), and the flag text names the tier and its band instead of asserting a defect. Malaysia re-ran 3 flags -> 2: P1068 was a false positive; P1065 and P1067 survive and were both then resolved by research with NO length change. The seven prior batches' route_integrity.json files were deliberately NOT regenerated — that would desync staged JSON from already-delivered workbooks — so in a pre-2026-08-12 packet check RouteAccuracy before trusting a length_ratio flag. Suspect flags per delivered packet: pakistan-gas 12 of 13, iraq-gas 9 of 12, india-gas 20 of 37, egypt-gas 6 of 13, kazakhstan-gas 2 of 10, libya-gas 1 of 11.

title: P1066 Operator = 'PETRONAS Carigali Sdn Bhd' is ONE of two defensible readings — staged medium, do not apply without settling the direction of the 2017 O&M agreement
summary: The only value change this packet stages is P1066's Operator (blank -> PETRONAS Carigali Sdn Bhd), on the operators/owners tab, tier MEDIUM. Neither source says 'operator' verbatim. The 2017 milestone appears on PETRONAS GAS BERHAD's OWN 'Our Journey' timeline: 'Execution of a 20-year O&M Agreement with PETRONAS Carigali Sdn Bhd for operation and maintenance of the SSGP'. The natural reading of a company listing that among its own achievements is that PGB WON the O&M contract and PCSB is the asset-owning counterparty — i.e. the operator-of-record would be PGB, the opposite of the staged value. The 2025 trade-press item puts PCSB in the decommissioning-executor role, which is an asset-owner function as much as an operator one. The third defensible answer is to leave Operator blank, which is what 81.6% of GGIT gas rows do (fill rate 22.53% tracker-wide, 18.44% on gas) — so a blank Operator here is the tracker norm and NOT a Malaysia defect, unlike India where it was a genuine gap. Reviewer's call; all three readings are stated in the row's ResearcherNotes.
